doc: Observation vocabulary per flow. The client re-observes and re-reports EVERY predicate on EVERY 'what's next' call — nothing is remembered client-side, and the service never asks for a value. Booleans only. `ownership` says who the fact belongs to: a local-fact is observed by the CLI (the CLI owns the answer — it is never a filesystem probe by another process) and may steer SEQUENCING only, never authorization; a server-fact is owned by the service and is authoritative even when the client can see something that looks like it.

targetDirValid.definition: The onboard target path exists and is a directory the client can read.
targetDirValid.why: ADDED. Nothing validates targetDir today: buildPlan takes it verbatim (the onboarding plan builder (capy-cli src/flows/onboard/plan.ts):81) and every reader is an existsSync that simply returns null for a path that is not there (the onboarding edit computation (capy-cli src/flows/onboard/edits.ts):35, :72, :115), so a typo'd or nonexistent directory produces a cheerful empty plan instead of a refusal. HANDOFF bug 3.
targetDirValid.source: the onboarding plan builder (capy-cli src/flows/onboard/plan.ts):81; the onboarding edit computation (capy-cli src/flows/onboard/edits.ts):35,72,115

hasCapyDir.definition: `.capy/` exists in the target directory (the gitignored local cache: `branch`, `sync-state.json`).
hasCapyDir.why: BASE. Deliberately NOT a proxy for 'initialized': detectProjectState keys initialization off keep.lock alone (packages/cli/src/core/projectManager.ts:17,45), while `.capy/` is created much earlier — writeSyncStateUserId runs immediately after authentication, before org selection (packages/cli/src/commands/capyCommand.ts:403-405, projectManager.ts:225). So a run that died at the redeem dead end leaves .capy/ with no keep.lock.

hasKeepLock.definition: A `keep.lock` FILE EXISTS in the target directory. Parse-independent: `existsSync` and nothing else.
hasKeepLock.why: BASE. The single fact detectProjectState turns into `initialized` (projectManager.ts:17,45) and therefore the fact capyCommand.ts:122 branches the whole first-run tree on. DELIBERATELY parse-independent: if a corrupt keep.lock reported false, the table would route to write_keep_lock(select_or_create) and offer to initialize OVER a git-owned file, with safety left to the executor noticing in time. Existence alone means no row of the table can ever propose overwriting it; corruption instead surfaces as the keep_lock_corrupt outcome of the first step that has to READ it (write_capy_dir / wrap_run_commands / encrypt_env), where the answer is blocked, never a write.

envMetaRecoverable.definition: `.env` carries the capy header comment lines (`# capy:org_id`, `# capy:project_id`, `# capy:branch`).
envMetaRecoverable.why: ADDED. This is the .env-header recovery branch: with org_id AND project_id in the header, capyCommand.ts:124-129 flips `initialized` back to true and skips first-run entirely even though keep.lock is missing. Without this predicate the flow cannot tell 'keep.lock was deleted, rebuild it' from 'this repo has never been onboarded', and would re-initialize a second project over a live one. The header is written by the same call that encrypts the file, so it also implies the .env has been encrypted at least once.

envStillPlaintext.definition: A `.env` exists AND at least one of its values does not start with `capy:`. No .env at all, or a fully encrypted one, is FALSE.
envStillPlaintext.why: BASE. Exactly the test backupPlaintextEnv already makes to decide whether there is anything to protect (packages/cli/src/files/fileManager.ts:400-405), and the same `startsWith('capy:')` line the init path uses to sort values (capyCommand.ts:777). Defining 'no .env' as false is deliberate: both 'nothing to encrypt' cases must sequence identically, and capyCommand.ts:764-766,978 already treats them the same.

commandsWrapped.definition: Every local edit the onboard plan computes for this directory is already applied — i.e. computeRunWrapEdits + computeAgentDocsEdits yield only `noop` edits. A directory the plan computes NO edits for is vacuously TRUE. Note the agent-instructions edit is not conditional on an agent file already existing: when none of the candidates is present the plan creates AGENTS.md, so a fresh directory reports FALSE and flips true once the verb has run.
commandsWrapped.why: BASE. The wrap is detected, not remembered: WRAPPED_RE decides 'already wrapped' per script (the onboarding edit computation (capy-cli src/flows/onboard/edits.ts):24,52,64) and apply.ts skips on noop / already-applied (the onboarding edit writer (capy-cli src/flows/onboard/apply.ts):31,52). The vacuous-true rule exists so a repo the plan computes nothing for terminates instead of looping on a verb that can never flip a predicate.
commandsWrapped.source: the onboarding edit computation (capy-cli src/flows/onboard/edits.ts):24,52,64,102-109; the onboarding edit writer (capy-cli src/flows/onboard/apply.ts):28-59; the onboarding plan builder (capy-cli src/flows/onboard/plan.ts):81

branchConflict.definition: `.env`'s header branch and `.capy/branch` both exist, disagree, and the `.capy/branch` side names a branch that really exists.
branchConflict.why: ADDED. Today this is a hard `process.exit(1)` with two recovery commands printed (packages/cli/src/commands/capyCommand.ts:183-184,250-285) — an interrupted checkout. It must become blocked{branch_conflict} rather than an exit code, and it must be observed BEFORE any write step, because every write step downstream needs a branch and would otherwise pick the wrong one. Note the stale-cache case is NOT a conflict: when .capy/branch names no real branch the .env header simply wins and the cache is rebuilt (capyCommand.ts:273-277), so this predicate is false there.

sessionLive.definition: A capy session usable for this org exists on this machine.
sessionLive.why: BASE. Server-fact even though the client can see it. The SERVICE'S OWN VIEW ALWAYS WINS: it is derived from the credential presented on the request together with the instance binding (an identified caller has a verified session by construction; an anonymous instance has none until its ceremony is claimed and the instance is rebound). The client's boolean is a HINT that may steer sequencing only — a client reporting `true` with no credential on the request gets the service's `false`, and a client reporting `false` while presenting a valid JWT gets the service's `true`. The client's honest observation comes from the CLI, never a filesystem probe — `capy info --json` (the sandbox-session ceremony client:124-127), the CLI-owns-the-answer doctrine.

orgKeyOnDevice.definition: The org named by keep.lock (or the .env header when keep.lock is absent) has its master key on this device: hasOrgKey(orgId, userId) is true. VACUOUSLY TRUE when no org is locally named (no keep.lock and no .env header) or when there is no session yet (no userId to check hasOrgKey against).
orgKeyOnDevice.why: ADDED, post-live-E2E (2026-08-17). HANDOFF-successor bug D: on a second machine with keep.lock present but this device never having received the org's master key (CAP-382 Case C), the table used to route authenticate -> write_capy_dir -> done, and the first `capy run` afterwards failed with 'no access to this project's secrets on this device' (packages/cli/src/crypto/keyResolver.ts, the syncProject access check) — the flow never modeled Case C as a step at all. capyCommand.ts:517-559 already runs the Case-C device-key unlock ceremony (attemptCaseCUnlock) inline during authentication; this predicate is what lets the table offer that same ceremony explicitly, as its own step, when a live session still finds the key missing.

ceremonyPending.definition: This flow instance holds an unconsumed, unexpired broker connection.
ceremonyPending.why: BASE, and the one predicate the client must NOT report: it is exactly the in-flight state that is not locally observable and that the SPEC requires to live with the flow instance. Today it lives in a module-level cache in the MCP process (the sandbox-session ceremony client:100-101), so a restarted process re-runs createConnection and mints a NEW user_code for a ceremony the human is still looking at — HANDOFF bug 2. The service reads it off the connections row (status='pending' AND expires_at > now()).
ceremonyPending.source: the sandbox-session ceremony client:100-107,155-165,282-323; the service's connection broker:902-995

compatible.why_excluded: Decided once, at instance creation, from findings the caller supplies; an incompatible project yields an instance that is created terminal-blocked{incompatible_project}. It is not re-observable per call and never changes mid-flow.

planApproved.why_excluded: Consent is instance state, not an observation — the same class as ceremony state, and it is what replaces the in-process planStore (plan.ts:74). It is applied as a gate in front of the ONBOARDING WRITE steps only (see steps.json `requires_consent` per verb), not as a predicate, so the predicate table stays a pure function of what the client can observe. See docs/flows/onboard-flow.md.

not_local_only.rule: The client MUST NOT create a flow instance when the CLI is in local-only mode, and MUST stay on the existing local path.
not_local_only.why: Local-only mode is an offline path with a synthetic org and no server of any kind: identity is the fixed local/local pair and the master key is unwrapped from a passphrase session (capyCommand.ts:130-134, :303-324, :1300-1314, config/profileConfig.ts isLocalOnly). A flow API call would be both impossible (no credential, no org) and wrong (the whole point is that this machine talks to nobody). Same class as `capy run` on cached state and `capy decrypt`: permanently off this layer.

report_schema.doc: The body of POST /flows/:id/next. The client re-observes and re-reports EVERY local fact on every call; nothing is remembered client-side. Booleans and codes only — never a value. `ceremonyPending` is FORBIDDEN, not merely optional: it is the one predicate the client cannot honestly observe, and `additionalProperties: false` on `observations` is what rejects it.

result.description: IDS AND NAMES a step resolved, which the service pins on the instance so a retry cannot resolve them a second time (a second project, a second branch). Never a value. Carried on a FAILED outcome too, and deliberately: a step that created the project and then died is exactly the case the pin exists for — losing the id there is what lets the next attempt create a second project.

code.description: Closed set. Every member except KEY_NOT_ON_DEVICE and FLOW_STOP_UNREACHABLE is an existing code: ERROR_CODES (the service's error codes, packages/cli/src/types/index.ts:317-347) or AUTH_CODES (the agent server's auth outcome codes). KEY_NOT_ON_DEVICE is minted here because today that condition is thrown as a generic AUTH_FAILED (capyCommand.ts:552) and would be indistinguishable from an ordinary auth failure — mint the code where the condition is first known rather than sniff it downstream. FLOW_STOP_UNREACHABLE is reported when an agent-driven run reaches a stop only a human could answer (no TTY, no local browser) — it is a real step outcome, and omitting it from this enum turned an actionable coded failure into a schema rejection. The mapping from code to blocked reason is in steps.json `blocked_reasons[].from_codes`.

plan.description: The freshly computed plan, sent only when the client found it no longer matches the one the instance holds. The service replaces the stored plan and CLEARS any recorded consent, so the next step is the dialog again — a human who approved one set of edits is never taken to have approved a different one. Names, paths, counts and a hash only.

project_name.description: OPTIONAL (CAP-451). The project NAME the plan targets, when the client already knows one. A client that folds this into its own plan_hash gets a rename to produce a different hash and re-open consent, the same way any other plan edit does. The org, by contrast, is never covered by plan_hash: it is pinned once (from an `authenticate` step's own result, verified against real membership) and a later report naming a different org is refused outright rather than reconciled through a plan change — see steps.json dialogs.onboard_plan.params_schema.properties.org_id.
